subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which term describes a melody supported by chords moving in the same rhythm?
questions.explain: Homophonic texture is a clear melody accompanied by chords.

questions.q: A chromatic scale moves entirely in:
questions.explain: A chromatic scale ascends or descends entirely in semitones, using all twelve pitches.

questions.q: How many different pitches does a pentatonic scale contain?
questions.explain: A pentatonic scale is made up of five different pitches per octave.

questions.q: A major triad is built from which intervals above the root?
questions.explain: A major triad stacks a major 3rd then a minor 3rd, giving a bright sound.

questions.q: What does the time signature 3/4 tell you?
options: Three beats in a bar, each a crotchet
Three beats in a bar, each a quaver
Four beats in a bar, each a crotchet
questions.explain: In 3/4 there are three crotchet beats per bar, giving a waltz feel.

questions.q: 'Imitation' as a way of developing an idea means:
options: One part copies a melodic idea just stated by another part
questions.explain: Imitation is when one part copies a melodic idea introduced by another part.

questions.q: On a string instrument, the technique 'pizzicato' means to:
options: Pluck the strings with the finger
questions.explain: Pizzicato instructs the player to pluck the strings rather than bow them.

questions.q: A rondo form is best described by which pattern?
questions.explain: In rondo form a main theme (A) returns between contrasting episodes, e.g. ABACA.

questions.q: Why is tuning important before an ensemble performs?
options: So all players sound in pitch with each other
questions.explain: Tuning ensures all players' pitches match so the ensemble sounds in tune together.

questions.q: The tempo marking 'andante' indicates a speed that is:
questions.explain: Andante means at a walking pace, a moderate tempo between slow and fast.

questions.q: Which Italian dynamic term means 'very quiet'?
questions.explain: Pianissimo (pp) means very quiet, whereas fortissimo (ff) means very loud.

questions.q: A plagal cadence (often called the 'Amen' cadence) is:
questions.explain: A plagal cadence moves from chord IV to chord I.

questions.q: What does 'a tempo' mean after a passage that has slowed down?
questions.explain: 'A tempo' instructs the performer to return to the original speed after a change.

questions.q: How many beats does a dotted minim last in 4/4 time?
questions.explain: A dot adds half the note's value, so a minim (2 beats) plus its dot (1 beat) lasts three beats.

questions.q: 'Polyphonic' (or contrapuntal) texture means:
options: Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together
questions.explain: Polyphonic texture combines two or more independent melodic lines.

questions.q: In music technology, 'panning' a sound controls:
options: Its position between the left and right speakers
questions.explain: Panning places a sound in the stereo field, between the left and right speakers.

questions.q: Compared with a major scale, a (natural) minor key generally sounds:
questions.explain: Minor keys typically sound darker or sadder than the brighter major.

questions.q: 'Sight-reading' means:
options: Playing music you have not seen before, at first sight
questions.explain: Sight-reading is performing a piece of music you are seeing for the first time.

questions.q: Repeating a short melodic pattern at higher or lower pitches in turn is called a:
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic idea at successively higher or lower pitches.

questions.q: A 'click track' used when recording provides:
options: A guide beat to keep performers in time
questions.explain: A click track is a steady metronome beat in the headphones that keeps performers in time while recording.

questions.q: When structuring a composition, why might a composer reuse a melodic idea in a contrasting section?
options: To create unity while still providing variety
questions.explain: Reusing ideas in new contexts gives a piece unity while contrast keeps it interesting.

questions.q: What does the dynamic marking 'mezzo-forte' (mf) mean?
questions.explain: Mezzo-forte means moderately loud, sitting between piano and forte.
